business_scope.primary_industry_name: GPS-Sealed Bonded Road Feeder Service for International Airports

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Egypt (national level, registered through the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones, GAFI)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid civil-law system with Islamic Sharia as a principal source of legislation; unitary national jurisdiction with no sub-tax autonomy

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering, as amended, and its Executive Regulations issued by Prime Ministerial Decree No. 95/2003; Central Bank of Egypt AML/CFT rules; Unified Companies Law No. 159 of 1981; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017; Law No. 34/1976 on Commercial Register; and the administrative supervisory powers of the State Council over company registers.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport copy of each UBO and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority of the UBO's country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Egypt is not party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency / Certificate of Good Standing of foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Egypt and the Egyptian consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney for the Egyptian incorporation agent
Bank reference letter confirming banking relationship and source of funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed financial institution maintaining the corporate account

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Arabic translation of the constitutional documents and UBO declaration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization before an Egyptian notary; consular legalization not required for domestically issued documents

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and signatories against OFAC SDN, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions, EU and UK HM Treasury financial sanctions, Egypt's terrorist entity designations, and EMLTFU/CBE internal watchlists; mandatory PEP identification, including foreign PEPs and close associates, with enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth/background review, and re-screening at least every 90 days.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI online investor services portal at www.gafi.gov.eg together with the Commercial Registry Directorate of the Ministry of Trade and Industry (paper filing at the competent district commercial registry)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be registered in Arabic script and be pronounceable in Arabic; a Latin-script transliteration may be filed as a secondary name, but the Arabic form is controlling for legal identity. The name must be distinctive, not identical or confusingly similar to existing registered names, and must comply with public-order restrictions on misleading names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant has 15 working days from the written rejection date to file a reconsideration request before the GAFI Investor Support/Grievance Committee, or the competent Commercial Registry Director, attaching the rejection notice, proposed name, legalized UBO documents, and a USD 50 reconsideration voucher; the registry must respond within 15 working days. If rejected again, the applicant may file an administrative appeal before the State Council (Administrative Court) within 60 days of the second refusal; legal representation by a member of the Egyptian Bar is required in the administrative appeal stage.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as a stand-alone registered seat for the licensed customs-bonded trucking LLC. GAFI and the Egyptian Customs Authority require a physical address in Egypt capable of receiving official service, storing company records, and supporting Customs/administrative inspections. A serviced office may be accepted only if it provides dedicated, staffed office space, not a virtual mailbox.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High — approximately 70% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection during the first 12 months after initial licensing and at least annually thereafter, because the customs bonded feeding service license triggers facility and fleet examination by the Customs Authority and the Ministry of Transport.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 149 of 2019, as amended, Articles 62–101 (LLC provisions) and 197–218 (registration); Executive Regulations issued by Decree No. 96 of 2020; Commercial Registry Law No. 34 of 1976; Customs Law No. 207 of 2020 for bonded road transport.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Companies Registration and Commercial Registry Directorate; commercial registration completed through GAFI One-Stop Shop.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation application submitted through GAFI with notarized Arabic Articles of Association (Memorandum of Association) and the executive regulations incorporation form.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an LLC under Law 149/2019. All quotas must be fully subscribed in the Articles; the declared capital must be deposited into an Egyptian licensed bank account opened for the company before incorporation, and the bank certificate of deposit must be submitted to GAFI. The funds are immobilized until the incorporation certificate is issued.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation contract, capital schedule, and Articles of Association submitted to GAFI are ratified. RESOLVED, that the quota subscriptions shown in the capital schedule are accepted and confirmed as fully paid, and the Board approves the registered capital as stated. RESOLVED, that the registered office address contained in the Articles is adopted as the company's legal seat for statutory purposes. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed General Manager and [Name] is appointed Company Secretary, each authorized to act individually in submitting regulatory filings, opening bank accounts, and applying for the customs bonded operating license.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve legal name and open capital deposit account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Investor Services (Name Reservation and One-Stop Shop) / Egyptian licensed bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three proposed Arabic/Latin names in GAFI's online portal or at GAFI center. After preliminary clearance, open a corporate capital account in an Egyptian bank in the company name. Deposit declared capital and obtain an unconditional capital deposit certificate. Foreign shareholders must legalize powers of attorney through the Egyptian embassy/consulate and provide certified passport copies.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID of each shareholder
Notarized power of attorney if an agent signs
Proposed registered office address or lease
Bank KYC documents for capital account opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a proposed name is rejected for being identical or misleading, file the next alternative within the same application or amend the spelling; no new capital deposit is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and notarize the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Justice Notary Public Office / sworn translator
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute Arabic Articles of Association before a notary public. All subscribers or lawful attorneys must appear, sign, and have signatures notarized. Translate any non-Arabic corporate documents into Arabic and attach legalized translations. Ensure the Articles contain the LLC name, purpose, registered office, capital quotas, governance, and manager powers required by Law 149/2019.
required_dossiers: Final Articles of Association in Arabic
Valid passports/IDs of all shareholders and managers
Certified translations of foreign shareholder corporate documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary notes a missing mandatory clause, submit a corrected signature page approved by all shareholders; notarial fees may be paid again.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit incorporation file and obtain Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Companies Registration and Commercial Registry Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete notarized dossier to the GAFI One-Stop Shop; pay registration and publication fees. GAFI examines legal formalities and, upon clearance, issues the Certificate of Incorporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a deficiency notice, rectify and resubmit within 30 days; if the activity requires a customs sector pre-approval, obtain conditional approval and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register in Commercial Registry and publish incorporation notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registry Office (GAFI / Ministry of Justice) and official publication unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the incorporation certificate is granted, file for the Commercial Registration certificate under Law 34/1976. Pay registry fees and arrange publication of the incorporation notice in the Egyptian Companies Gazette. Obtain the Commercial Registration number and registry extract.
required_dossiers: Tax card application receipt if already issued
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Registry rejects due to a mismatch between the manager civil ID or lease, correct the underlying document and pay the amendment filing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for tax, VAT, payroll, and social insurance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) – Taxpayer Services; National Social Insurance Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the Tax Card via the ETA portal or taxpayer service center. Register for VAT if the company's taxable supplies meet the threshold. Register employees with the Social Insurance Authority and obtain the employer workflow and labor inspection references.
required_dossiers: Lease or ownership proof for premises
Workforce list and employment contract template
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If ETA rejects because address verification is pending, provide a utility bill and notarized lease; escalate through the GAFI investor complaints unit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Apply for Customs Bonded Carrier License for truck fleet
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Customs Authority (ECA) – Customs Transit and Bonded Transport Licensing Directorate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a customs transporter license application authorizing sealed road feeder operations between airports and bonded warehouses. Include fleet inventory, GPS tracking and e-seal system, customs guarantee, driver and vehicle security files. Pass inspection of sealing equipment and depot. Upon approval, receive the Customs Bonded Transporter ID and operating conditions.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and tax card
Vehicle title certificates or long-term lease contracts
GPS and electronic seal specifications certified by an ECA-approved vendor
Security clearance for drivers and operational staff
Depot, garage, and parking address with Civil Defense approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If ECA requires stronger security guarantees, increase the bank guarantee or add an insurance rider; if equipment fails inspection, replace it and submit proof of compliance for reinspection. If the license is denied, appeal to the Customs Authority Dispute Committee within 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain airport operator access and civil defense/manpower clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Civil Aviation Authority / Airport cargo operator; Civil Defense Authority; Ministry of Manpower
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for landside or non-airside access permits for feeder trucks at the relevant international airport cargo village. File vehicle and driver information with airport security. Undergo Civil Defense inspection of the depot, office, and loading dock; obtain workplace safety clearance. Ensure drivers hold airport security passes.
required_dossiers: Firefighting equipment list and maintenance record
Facility land use and lease documents
Insurance certificates covering cargo and third-party liability
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If airport access is denied due to security gaps, implement the required CCTV, escort, and electronic-seal procedures and reapply; if Civil Defense flags non-compliance, correct firefighting and storage conditions and request re-inspection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Egyptian Customs Authority (ECA) for customs bonded transport; General Authority for Roads, Land and Dry Ports for road transport operations; Egyptian Civil Aviation Authority for airport-adjacent feeder operations.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Customs Bonded Road Feeder Operator's License; Road Transport Operator Permit; Airport Cargo Village Access Permit.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B – Limited Environmental Assessment / registration screening under Law No. 4/1994 as amended by Law No. 9/2009; a full EIA report is not normally required for a bonded truck fleet, but screening must be completed for depot and fuel-storage installations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Fleet diesel engines must comply with EEAA exhaust emission limits for PM, NOx, and CO; vehicles shall meet applicable fuel standards and roadworthy smoke-opacity thresholds. Wastewater from washing bays shall be treated or disposed of through licensed operations; solid waste and used oils handled in accordance with Waste Management Law No. 147 of 2020. Bonded trailers are sealed and compartmentalized to prevent spillage of dust, cargo residue, or hazardous substances during transport.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the Civil Defense Authority; structural safety inspection of the depot, warehouse, and administrative premises; Occupational Health and Workplace Clearance from the Ministry of Manpower; drivers' periodic medical fitness certificates and airport security clearances from the Egyptian Civil Aviation Authority.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) under the Egyptian Ministry of Finance; official filing portal: Egypt E-Invoice / E-Tax Portal at https://einvoicing.eta.gov.eg and https://www.eta.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Egyptian LLC must register with the ETA after incorporation and issuance of the commercial registry certificate. Submission of incorporation documents, articles of association, board resolution appointing local tax representative, proof of registered address, and shareholder identification. The ETA issues a Tax Identification Number (TIN) and VAT certificate. For bonded trucking, the LLC must be licensed as a customs carrier and obtain an authorized economic operator (AEO) status where applicable. Registration may be initiated online through the ETA portal followed by physical verification at the tax office.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt does not apply US-style check-the-box elections. A domestic LLC is automatically taxed as a separate entity under Law No. 91 of 2005 and Law No. 67 of 2016 (VAT). Available statutory elections include the election to join or leave a corporate tax group (fiscal unity) subject to ministerial conditions, the election to apply the simplified Cash-Basis regime for small taxpayers below the EGP 10 million turnover threshold, and available hybrid mismatch alignment elections permitted by local transfer-pricing documentation rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual taxable turnover for supplies of goods and services; mandatory VAT registration is required for any person engaged in importing or exporting goods regardless of turnover, and for any person contracting with government entities where such supplies are subject to VAT
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Egypt mandates phased continuous electronic invoicing and e-receipt for taxpayers above specified revenue thresholds. Invoices for B2B supplies must be issued, transmitted, and digitally stamped through the ETA e-invoicing platform in the required JSON/XML schema. Clearance is real-time using a unique QR code and digital signature; integration is required through an ERP-to-ETA API web service or approved tax authority portal. Customs bonded trucking operators must synchronise electronic tax invoices with Customs System (NACIS) and the e-invoicing system to evidence exempt/zero-rated export transactions and customs bonded movements.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to physical export of goods outside Egypt, directly exported or deemed exported, and to international transport services directly related to exported goods, when the service provider is a registered taxable person and the supply is evidenced by customs documentation. For customs bonded road feeder services that move airport cargo under customs seal, zero-rating is recognised if the transport is in connection with an exportation of goods and the operator retains the customs bonded movement document proving exit from Egypt. Services ancillary to transport within Egypt are in principle subject to VAT unless supplied directly to an exporter as part of an export transaction satisfying documentary tests.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/Data from NACIS containing export invoice number, HS codes, and net masse)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (often accompanied by Customs Bonded Movement Register / TIR Carnet where applicable)
Inward Remittance Certificate or Foreign Currency Bank Statement proving payment for exported goods has been received in Egypt
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is strictly scrutinised by the ETA using cross-validation of customs export declarations, international transport documents, banking settlement data, and the e-invoicing system. Fraudulent or abusive zero-rating claims expose the taxpayer to clawback of the entire VAT input credit claimed, an additional tax of 14% on the under-declared supply, a fine of not less than 50% and not exceeding 150% of the due tax, late payment interest, criminal sanctions for forging customs or remittance documents, and possible AEO licence revocation plus blacklisting from all customs bonded operations.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) — the sole monetary and foreign-exchange authority under Law No. 88 of 2003 and the Exchange Control Law No. 80 of 1947; supervises all authorized dealer banks, administers the EGP unified flexible exchange-rate regime adopted on March 6, 2024, and enforces Egypt's IMF Article VIII current-account convertibility obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt maintains IMF Article VIII convertibility for all bona fide current-account transactions, including cross-border service-export earnings of the GPS-sealed bonded truck fleet business; such inflows are freely creditable to Egyptian accounts and no prior CBE approval is required for current-account settlement. Capital-account convertibility is treaty-protected and legally available for foreign equity, shareholder loans, dividend repatriation, and capital disinvestment, but is subject to documentary gates: GAFI investment registration, an authorized-dealer banking channel, audited financial statements, and a final tax-clearance certificate from the Egyptian Tax Authority. Practical hurdles persist in foreign-currency priority queues during periodic liquidity tightening and strict bank-level verification of the underlying commercial documentation; however, the 2024 liberalization, the settlement of approximately USD 2.1 billion of overdue investor FX arrears, and the IMF Extended Fund Facility have materially removed prior convertibility rationing, and profit remittance is now processed at the unified market rate.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Post-March 2024 deregulation: the mandatory conversion ratio is 0% — the earlier 50% to 75% surrender circulars of 2022-2023 were repealed, and exporters may lawfully retain export earnings in foreign currency in Egyptian bank accounts or convert at the unified market rate without CBE-imposed conversion quotas. Statutory repatriation timeline: export and service-export proceeds must be routed through an authorized dealer bank in Egypt within a maximum of 5 months from the date of shipment or service performance; deferred-payment arrangements may extend to 8 months only with prior CBE approval evidenced in the bank file. For bonded road-feeder operations to international airports, all freight and logistics service income is treated as invisible export proceeds and must be accompanied by CMR/AWB documentation so that the receiving bank can verify the export nexus and record the inflow in CBE reporting systems.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: EGP Current Account + USD Foreign-Currency Operational Account (dual-account structure)
EGP Operational Account + USD Export Proceeds Collection Account
Multi-Currency Corporate Current Account with Trade Finance Package (LC and Collections)
Export Proceeds Collection and Receivables Settlement Account
EGP Operational Account + USD Settlement Sub-Account
Capital Escrow / Foreign-Shareholder Remittance Account (EGP-USD paired)
USD Operational Account with Cross-Border Clearing Access

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a primary inbound settlement or repatriation rail; Medium only as an ancillary disbursement channel. Legal constraints: a non-licensed offshore EMI cannot hold EGP, cannot act as an authorized dealer for Egyptian service-export receipts, and cannot satisfy the CBE obligation to repatriate invisible earnings through an Egyptian banking institution; using an offshore EMI as the collecting account for cross-border transport fees would constitute a circumvention of the Exchange Control Law No. 80/1947 and the CBE Payment Systems Law No. 18/2019 licensing regime. Permitted usage is limited to post-tax operational disbursements such as paying non-resident software or contracted services, provided the underlying invoices are booked in Egypt and the outbound payment is executed through an authorized bank with proper tax documentation.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-person onboarding is mandatory. At least one Egyptian-resident director or the General Manager must appear at the bank branch with original commercial registration, tax card, company seal, certified Memorandum and Articles of Association, and a notarized board resolution appointing signatories. The ultimate beneficial owner may appear personally or through a notarized and consular-legalized power of attorney, but a face-to-face compliance interview with the corporate KYC officer is mandatory before account activation. No Egyptian tier-1 bank permits fully remote account opening for a cross-border freight and logistics entity as of 2025; video-KYC is accepted only as a supplement to the branch interview, never as a substitute.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume same-day USD/EGP transaction pattern inconsistent with the truck-fleet operating cycle (structuring red flag)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed transport contracts with airlines and regulated freight forwarders; per-trip CMR waybills and TIR customs-bonded transit documents; GPS geofence and route-audit log exports; trip-level invoice-to-waybill reconciliation ledger; fuel and toll receipts from licensed suppliers; driver logbook and fleet register.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border service-export inflows without a clear SWIFT purpose code matching the corporate registry's declared activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: IATA Cargo Account Settlement System (CASS) statements; master and house airway bills with airport customs-bonded terminal attestations; CBE service-export notification and commercial-invoice references; per-voyage revenue ledger and audited service-revenue allocation schedule.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity or unregistered non-resident shareholders under consolidated AML/CFT due-diligence rules
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: GAFI incorporation certificate; notarized and apostilled or consular-legalized shareholders' ledger and register extracts; certified passport copies of all UBOs; SWIFT proof of capital inflow matched to the Egyptian receiving bank's inward-remittance advice; 12-month audited financial statements and Egyptian Tax Authority compliance declarations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or PEP hits, or dual-use concern affecting counterparties using bonded corridors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: AVS/World-Check/OFAC-UN-EU sanctions screening outputs with risk-rating memorandum; end-user and end-use certificates under Egyptian customs protocols; HS-code and dual-use classification attestations; IATA freight-partner corroboration; trade-lane justification memorandum describing the bonded feeder corridor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Delay in repatriating service-export proceeds beyond the CBE statutory window (5 months, or 8 months only with prior approval)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dated CMR/AWB evidence; debtor aging schedule for air-cargo counterparties; SWIFT MT103 inflow records; CBE export-proceeds registration printouts; where non-performance occurred, a legal claim file, insurer indemnity documentation, and bank-validated offset and netting agreements.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inward shareholder equity injections must flow exclusively through the banking system: the foreign investor initiates a SWIFT MT103 transfer to the Egyptian authorized dealer bank's correspondent account, and the Egyptian bank credits the company's USD sub-account and files the CBE inward-remittance statistical return. The company must simultaneously register the inflow with GAFI (FDI project registration or share-capital amendment) and with the CBE investment-registration records, using the purpose designation 'Contribution to share capital of Egyptian LLC, GAFI registered', accompanied by the Commercial Registration number and Egyptian IBAN. The company must retain for the statutory five-year period the inward-remittance advice, the MT103 message, and the bank conversion certificate if the USD was converted to EGP. There is no physical fungible exchange; settlement is cleared via SWIFT USD/EUR/GBP correspondent clearing through the CBE, with value dating as instructed.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlement uses three coordinated rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 customer transfers for recurrent operating disbursements such as customs-bonded tolls, runway-side service fees, spare parts, and fuel, subject to bank-validated commercial invoices and CBE advance-cargo-information filing; (ii) commercial documentary letters of credit issued via SWIFT MT700 for high-value capital procurement including tractors, air-ride dollies, and telematics hardware, funded on 100% cash cover for imported capital goods; and (iii) documentary collections on documents-against-payment for low-value consumables. All outbound flows must mirror the National Single Window / NAFEZA customs declarations and CMR documentation, and each foreign-currency outflow is settled through the CBE-authorized interbank FX market and reported on the bank's CBE returns at T+1.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/EGP forward contracts with authorized dealer banks, supported by underlying service-export invoices or import obligations and settled on actual flows;
Spot-forward FX swap programmes with CBE-licensed banks to match airport-cargo monthly working-capital cycles;
Currency-neutral trade-receivables financing including USD-denominated factoring and forfaiting of air-cargo invoices to avoid EGP convertibility friction;
European-style FX options with CBE-authorized banks, with premium payable in EGP and optionality restricted to genuine economic exposure;

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts are not generally permissible onshore against EGP except with prior CBE approval for specific interbank applications; Egyptian corporates should treat NDFs as a restricted instrument requiring specialized bank and central bank authorization.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return with audited financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months of fiscal year-end (e.g., 30 April for calendar-year taxpayers)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty: 10% of tax liability plus 2% monthly interest; continued non-compliance may trigger enforced collection and administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual audited financial statements submitted to shareholders for approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Assembly of Shareholders (LLC corporate record)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of fiscal year-end, unless adjourned by written consent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Not a government filing; failure may expose managers to civil liability and court-ordered insolvency proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO/AML register audit and confirmation memorandum
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company share register / compliance file; available for GAFI and public prosecutor inspections
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Before 31 January of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Violation of AML Law No. 80/2002: administrative fines and/or criminal prosecution of responsible managers.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All Egyptian LLCs are legally obliged to appoint a licensed auditor and prepare audited financial statements, regardless of turnover; no size threshold exempts LLCs.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), aligned to IFRS, issued under Law No. 95 of 2015.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Egypt's AML Law (80/2002) and Companies Law 159/1981, each LLC must maintain an up-to-date share register and conduct an annual internal review to confirm the direct and indirect shareholding ownership chain, including natural-person beneficial owners, and record any changes in the minutes. No separate annual government UBO filing is required; information must be produced on demand.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No blanket tax holiday. Under Investment Law No. 72/2017, eligible investment projects in the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCEZ) and qualifying new industrial/logistics zones may enjoy a 50% reduction of net taxable profits for up to 5 years from commencement of activity. Standard capital allowances and depreciation deductions apply.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 19 (Income Tax Return for Legal Persons) submitted electronically through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) e-filing portal at www.eta.gov.eg
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return; quarterly advance tax prepayments due on 30 June, 30 September, 30 December and 30 April
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be filed within 4 months after the end of the fiscal year (e.g., 30 April for a calendar-year taxpayer).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross operating receipts from bonded trucking and airport feeder services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign non-resident company without an Egyptian PE must omit this field; where a PE exists, only Egypt-source revenue attributable to the PE is included.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct deductible expenses: fuel, fleet maintenance, customs bond charges, driver wages, insurance, depreciation, subcontracting costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses actually borne by the Egyptian PE are deductible. Head-office allocations must be arm's length and supported by transfer-pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit before tax after deducting allowable expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident taxpayer, this is the PE attributable profit under Art. 38 of Law 91/2005 after applying transfer-pricing adjustments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses carried forward from prior years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident's PE may offset its own prior losses within the 5-year carryforward limit, but treaty losses may not be imported to Egypt.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after loss offset and statutory adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Taxable base is subject to 22.5% corporate rate; treaty PE determination must be disclosed if the foreign company is claiming no PE.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: statutory fixed fine of EGP 5,000 – EGP 20,000; additional monthly delay fee of 2% of tax due (maximum 30% of the total tax amount); late payment interest at central bank rate plus surcharge; intentional non-filing triggers criminal sanctions under Art. 104 and Art. 107 of Law 91/2005.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident beneficial owner must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its country of residence, submit it to the Egyptian Tax Authority together with the official treaty relief form (Form 8 WHT application), declare the absence of a permanent establishment in Egypt, and obtain ETA clearance before the dividend distribution. If relief is not pre-cleared, the 10% domestic WHT is withheld at source and the non-resident may file a refund claim with the ETA within 5 years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory WHT for non-resident recipients: royalties 20%, interest 20%. Under Egypt's tax treaties, headline rates generally range from 10% to 20% for royalties and interest, and certain treaties provide a 0% rate for bank interest or official lending institutions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 1,000,000 annual aggregate controlled transactions for mandatory Local File; Master File is required for multinational groups with consolidated global revenue exceeding EGP 2,000,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) as in UAE or Bermuda. However, the Income Tax Law No. 91/2005 contains general anti-abuse provisions (Art. 98) and substance-over-form principles. The Egyptian LLC must maintain real management, offices, staff and physical truck operations in Egypt. Failing this, the ETA may recharacterize transactions, deny treaty benefits, and deem a taxable Egyptian PE.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of bonded transport revenues, use of forged invoices for fuel and maintenance, fictitious subcontracting to shell entities, and off-the-books cash carriage.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Art. 107 of Income Tax Law No. 91/2005: imprisonment for a term of 3 to 5 years and a fine of EGP 10,000 – EGP 50,000; plus assessed tax at 22.5%, late surcharges, delay interest, and seizure of trucks and logistics assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general managers who participate in or knowingly permit fraudulent accounting are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate tax; criminal conviction imposes travel bans, passport seizure and potential prison term until the tax debt is settled.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Egytian LLC used as a letterbox conduit to channel Suez Canal logistics profits to the foreign parent, without real truck fleets, employees, warehouse premises or decision-making in Egypt; contracts and management are solely offshore.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization under the general anti-avoidance rule (Art. 98) and transfer-pricing adjustment; the entire profit is deemed attributable to an Egyptian permanent establishment, taxed at 22.5%, with penalties up to 30% of adjusted tax and customs bond license cancellation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for reclassified taxes if they executed an artificial scheme known to be unlawful; veil piercing is granted by courts on proof of fraud, nominalism or abuse of legal personality; travel restrictions and administrative freezing orders may issue.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the customs bonded truck fleet to smuggle goods, duplicate bills of lading, funnel cash courier settlements into nominee bank accounts, and launder proceeds through repeated structured payments to avoid reporting thresholds under Anti-Money Laundering Law No. 80 of 2002.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment of 15 to 25 years and a fine between EGP 50,000 and EGP 5,000,000, confiscation of freight vehicles and funds; customs penalties up to 10 times the duty value for false declarations; licence and customs bond status permanently revoked.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners face pretrial detention, freezing orders, travel bans, and confiscation of assets traced to laundering; directors cannot escape liability by resigning if they had knowledge or control during the violation.
